conventions.convention: The grid is deterministic and strictly increasing; n,M≥1, B>0 and 0≤α<B. Loss rows take values in the Borel space [0,B]^M. Exchangeability means joint-law invariance under row permutations, without independence.
Loss nesting means nonincreasing loss along the grid. Endpoint safety means every terminal loss is at most α almost surely. Expected test risk averages over both calibration and test rows.
Test (sum of n calibration losses+B)/(n+1)≤α in increasing grid order, including equality; return the first passing rule, or the maximum-grid rule with fallback status if none passes.
Conditional risk control requires a supplied actual regular conditional distribution of the full matrix, with exchangeability and the applicable loss hypotheses holding sectionwise almost surely.
The monotone envelope at index j is the maximum over indices k≥j, including j and M.
Multilabel sets use scores ≥1−λ; the grid ends at λ=1, and the false-negative loss for an empty true-label set is zero.

load_bearing.statement: Every admissible algorithm input returns a unique output after at most M threshold tests, without monotonicity or endpoint safety. For exchangeable Borel [0,B]^M loss rows on a deterministic finite grid, with n,M≥1, B>0, 0≤α<B, almost-sure coordinatewise nonincrease and terminal losses ≤α, the selected test loss has expectation ≤α. The corresponding conditional inequality holds given a supplied regular conditional full-matrix law whose sections satisfy these hypotheses almost surely.

For bounded calibration losses on the supplied deterministic finite grid, return the first grid point and associated prediction rule satisfying (sum of calibration losses+B)/(n+1)≤α, with pass status; if none passes, return the maximum-grid rule with fallback status.

For exchangeable Borel [0,B]^M loss rows on a deterministic finite grid, with n,M≥1, B>0, 0≤α<B and terminal losses ≤α almost surely, calibrating the finite tail maxima gives expected original test loss ≤α, without original-row monotonicity. The conditional version holds under an actual sectionwise exchangeable regular conditional row law satisfying the same bounds and endpoint condition.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.2 defines j_*=min{j:S_j≤α} and then calls j_* a Borel function of the full matrix. Endpoint safety is only almost sure, so this set may be empty on an exceptional event and is empty for some matrices in the ambient Borel space. Specify a measurable default, such as j_*=M when the set is empty. This closes the global measurability detail used in 2.2; the risk argument remains valid almost surely.
